narr: A strong 500mb shortwave aided in the development of two thunderstorm complexes that impacted Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley on May 23rd and 24th. The first complex began shortly after 6 PM in Zapata County and inched southeastward across the region before becoming nearly stationary in Cameron and Willacy Counties around 2 AM on the morning of the 24th. This lead to numerous reports of flooding and several reports of damaging wind, especially in central Hidalgo County, where the worst of the damage was reported.||The second complex developed in northern Mexico and entered Zapata County around 4 AM on the morning of May 24th, which helped to spark several showers and storms ahead of it in Starr County. This is when there were several reports of hail. Also, additional flooding occurred in southern Hidalgo and Cameron Counties. By the time all was said and done, much of the Rio Grande Valley had picked up between 2 to 6 inches of rain, with locally higher 5 to 9 inches in parts of Zapata and Starr Counties.
ev: Social media pictures showed several submerged cars that were being removed from flood waters from the heavy rain the night before. Flood depth of 3 to 4 feet is estimated due to how high the water was on the cars.

Video on social media shows several feet of fast moving water near Medina Street - a flood-prone area known as Medina Addition - with two SUVs that had been swept off the road and into a ditch. Video later shows the vehicles getting dragged out of the ditch by a tow truck. Based on the during and after videos, it is estimated that 3 to 4 feet of fast flowing water was moving across the road at the height of the flash flooding. Additional video shows people having to abandon homes during the height of the flooding and the water coming up to their waists, which supports the 3 to 4 foot estimates of fast moving water. A report of 8 of rain came in from just northwest of Zapata from this storm. The local newspaper in Zapata County later reported that at least 15 homes were affected with many of them losing their furniture, clothing, and household items.
